attempted_claim: Does S^2 x S^2 admit a pair of strongly exotic codimension-1 embeddings that survives external stabilization? Precisely: do there exist a closed oriented 3-manifold Y and smooth embeddings i_1,i_2:Y -> S^2 x S^2 such that (i) i_1 and i_2 are topologically ambient isotopic, (ii) no smooth ambient isotopy carries i_1 to i_2, (iii) there is a diffeomorphism f:S^2 x S^2 -> S^2 x S^2 with f o i_1 = i_2 (diffeomorphic complements), and (iv) the pair remains smoothly non-isotopic after connected sum with any closed smooth 4-manifold performed away from i_1(Y) union i_2(Y), in particular after any number of S^2 x S^2 stabilizations?
decisive_failure: No stable smooth-isotopy theorem for codimension-1 embeddings in S^2 x S^2 is available in hand: Quinn 1986 Theorem 1.4 covers self-maps from smooth pseudoisotopies, and the Perron-Quinn and Galvin-Orson-Powell stabilization theorems cover surfaces only. Gauge-theoretic certificates vanish on the positive-scalar-curvature S^2 x S^2 background and under further S^2 x S^2 sums. Both literature calls were consumed verifying this gap, so no further lead can be checked in this pass.
